title: Massa Ranghar’s Sacrilege Sets Up the Next Retaliation

blocks.text: The late persecution episode is summarized through notorious names and local memory. Rama Randhawa’s territory becomes a proverb for danger, while stories circulate about villages where even travel feels more dangerous than surviving on wild food.

The page then names the outrage that will define the next turn of the narrative: Massa Ranghar desecrated the Darbar Sahib and other informers helped deliver Sikhs, including Bhai Taru Singh, into Mughal hands. The violence is now not only political but openly sacrilegious.

Finally the poem turns toward response. By introducing the episode of Mehtab Singh and Sukha Singh, it signals that the long record of complaint and persecution is about to give way to remembered Sikh retaliation against Massa Ranghar.
